title: Cleanroom Gowning: Dress Your Colleague
summary: Hand over the right garments, in the right order, and watch them go on.
story: Aseptic areas (where sterile medicines are filled) need stricter gowning than a normal production floor. Here you coach a colleague through it: pick each garment from the table and hand it over. Only cleanroom-approved items are allowed, so street clothes, watches and make-up have to stay out. Each garment goes on in a set order so that the cleanest items touch nothing dirty.

glossary.def: Done in a way that keeps everything sterile (free of living microbes), for example when filling injectable medicines.
A one-piece suit that covers the whole body so skin and clothing shed nothing into the room.
A speck of dust, skin or fibre. Cleanrooms count them, and people are the main source.
Gloves supplied germ-free. They go on last and are sanitised during work.
Any departure from the written procedure. In a regulated plant each one is recorded.
A tamper-evident record of who did what and when, so an inspector can verify the training happened.

steps.label: Hood
steps.instruction: Hand your colleague the sterile hood. It goes on first and must cover all hair.
steps.hazard: Hair and skin shed thousands of particles a minute; the hood contains them.
steps.wrongHint: Start with the hood: everything else is fitted over it.

steps.label: Face mask
steps.instruction: Now the face mask. It must cover the nose and chin.
steps.hazard: Breathing and speaking release droplets and microbes.
steps.wrongHint: The mask goes on straight after the hood.

steps.label: Coverall
steps.instruction: Pass the coverall. Your colleague steps into it without letting it touch the floor.
steps.hazard: A coverall that touches the floor is contaminated.
steps.wrongHint: The coverall comes after hood and mask, before shoe covers.

steps.label: Shoe covers
steps.instruction: Pass the shoe covers. They are fitted sitting on the bench, swinging each leg over the line.
steps.hazard: Dirty-side shoes must never touch the clean-side floor.
steps.wrongHint: Shoe covers go on after the coverall and before gloves.

steps.label: Sterile gloves
steps.instruction: Last of all: sterile gloves, pulled over the coverall cuffs.
steps.hazard: Gloves put on early get contaminated while dressing.
steps.wrongHint: Gloves are always last, once everything else is fitted.

distractors.label: Wristwatch
distractors.hint: Watches and jewellery shed particles and trap microbes. Nothing like that is allowed in a cleanroom.

distractors.label: Street jacket
distractors.hint: Street clothing carries dirt and fibres. It never goes past the changing line.

distractors.label: Make-up
distractors.hint: Cosmetics shed particles and are banned in cleanrooms.

quiz.text: Which of these may you wear into the cleanroom?

options: Sitting on the bench, over the line

quiz.text: Why do gloves go on last?
options: So they stay clean while dressing
